title: Global research trends in AI-related foot and ankle surgery research: A bibliometric and visualized study

reading.body:
AI research in foot and ankle surgery grew every year from 1999 to 2024, reaching 2,047 papers, with China leading on volume and the United States on impact.

The pattern is a field moving from method to application. Keyword analysis shows early work concentrated on foundational algorithms, then shifted toward lower limb kinematics and clinical disease. The two topics flagged as emerging are diabetic foot ulcers and computer-aided diagnosis. That progression is typical of a domain once the underlying techniques become available to clinicians rather than only to computer scientists.

The geographic split is the more interesting detail. China produced 581 papers with an H-index of 47. The United States produced 489 papers with an H-index of 53. Volume leadership and impact leadership sit in different countries, which means counting publications alone would misread who is shaping this research.

What this does not cover is compute. The study measures publications, citations, and keywords, not the hardware, data centers, or power those studies consumed. Nothing here indicates whether the imaging models behind computer-aided diagnosis run on local machines or large clusters, and nothing indicates how much electricity the field's training and inference demand. The data also stops at December 31, 2024, so any acceleration after that date is invisible. Read it as a map of research attention, not of infrastructure.

explain_beginner: This paper looks at how researchers have used artificial intelligence in foot and ankle surgery over time. The authors searched a large scientific database and found 2047 studies published between 1999 and 2024, with the number growing every year. China and the United States produced the most research. Early work focused on building the basic computer methods, and later work moved toward studying how legs move and treating real patients. The authors say two topics are likely to matter most going forward: diabetic foot ulcers and computer-aided diagnosis. This matters because it shows where medical AI is heading and who is leading the way.
explain_business: This study maps the growth of artificial intelligence research in foot and ankle surgery, based on 2047 publications from 1999 to 2024. Output is rising every year, and China and the United States dominate, though the United States shows stronger research impact per paper. The field has moved from basic algorithms to clinical applications, and the authors flag diabetic foot ulcers and computer-aided diagnosis as the areas most likely to grow. For decision makers, this signals where clinical and investment interest is concentrating, and it suggests that partnerships or hiring in these two areas, plus awareness of Chinese and American leadership, should shape research and product strategy.
explain_practitioner: The authors performed a bibliometric analysis of AI research in foot and ankle surgery, retrieving publications from the Web of Science Core Collection through December 31, 2024. They analyzed 2047 papers spanning 1999 to 2024 and visualized the data with VOSviewer and CiteSpace. Publication output rose steadily each year. China led in volume with 581 papers and an H-index of 47, while the United States had 489 papers and a higher H-index of 53. Keyword co-occurrence showed a shift from foundational algorithms toward lower limb kinematics and clinical disease applications. Burst analysis identified diabetic foot ulcers and computer-aided diagnosis as emerging hotspots.
